steps.content: The storm in the ceremony hall is growing more violent by the second, with fierce winds tearing through the entire castle, shredding everything into fractured light and swirling dust. You struggle toward the stairway, each step made on the edge of collapse, the path beneath your feet nearly vanishing in the windswept debris.

Rocks, debris, and unidentifiable objects hurtle chaotically through the storm, howling past your head and crashing everywhere. A sudden piercing sound comes dangerously close to the back of your head. You instinctively dodge to the side—and a split second later, the remains of a chandelier crash down, shattering into countless pieces at your feet.
You have no time to dwell on your close call. A single thought occupies your mind—you must reach the study and find that journal as quickly as possible.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Must move faster...

Gritting your teeth with determination, you clamber over a collapsed stone pillar and barely regain your footing when another violent gust of wind hurls a splintered wooden beam directly at you. You instantly drop into a low slide, your body skimming across the floor for several feet, narrowly avoiding the deadly fragment.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Almost there...
The study door is right ahead. You lunge forward and push it open, plant both feet against the wall to redirect your momentum, and roll smoothly into the room—
As you enter, you reach back to slam the door shut and lock it, temporarily sealing the storm outside.
Seeing the warm glow of light illuminating the walls and desk, you finally let out a breath of relief. Thankfully, this room remains completely intact, untouched by the storm's assault.

That series of death-defying maneuvers has completely drained your strength, but there's little time to recover. After a brief moment to catch your breath, you grasp a bookshelf for support and shakily rise to your feet, beginning your search for the journal that Graves took away.
Finally, in the corner of a toppled bookshelf, you spot the familiar black cover.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Phew... Thank goodness it's still here...
The journal remains open to the last page you were reading:
November 2, N.F. 89, Abandoned infant: unnamed Procurement list: milk powder, diapers, blankets...
After confirming it's the right journal, you swiftly grab it, but just as you're ready to tuck it away into your coat pocket, the entire study lurches violently.
Boom—!!

As a deafening boom rends the air, the storm breaches the sanctuary with ferocious intensity. Frenzied gusts hurl a barrage of debris into the room, causing the floor to convulse violently. Cracks race across the walls, picture frames shatter to the ground, and bookshelves emit shrill. In the next moment—
The weighty bookshelf comes crashing down directly toward you!
[Ceremony Hall]

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: For the love of heaven, please let this old architecture hold together!
Lumi shields the two monsters as they huddle in a corner.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Please be okay, my valued client! Don't tell me you left just to skip out on my commission fee! Come on, you wouldn't want to lose both the property and your dear agent—
[Attic]

The study now lies in ruins, reduced to nothing but collapsed rubble. Shattered wooden beams litter the floor, heavy bookshelves lay toppled in chaotic heaps, and fallen candelabras rest among the debris, their flames utterly extinguished.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Cough, cough...

Behind the collapsed bookshelves, the rubble shifts slightly as you struggle to push aside splintered wood and slowly rise from the debris. While your body is covered in scrapes, it's the years-old dust you've accidentally inhaled that truly makes you miserable.
You wave away the floating dust clouds, finally able to see what lies before you. Behind the study walls, hidden away and completely isolated from the outside world, is a small attic...

The cramped, confining space has a ceiling too low to stand upright, with floorboards creaking with each step as if they might give way at any moment. The walls are cobbled together from rough wooden planks, riddled with cracks and wormholes.

A shelf against the wall holds a few modest possessions: an oil lamp, a clay bowl, and a small box containing dried flower petals and ribbons. In the corner lies a small pile of fairy tale books, beside them sits a low stool, clearly cut down to accommodate the height of its user.

Nearby, a single bed, smaller than the standard size, stands strewn with patched-up old dresses, worn cloaks, and a threadbare blanket. In the dim glow of moonlight, several faded crayon drawings on the walls come into view.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Oh right, the journal.

With no time to dwell on this attic, your true purpose springs back to your mind. Amidst the chaos of the collapse, you lost hold of the journal, but luck is on your side—it lies nearby, its yellowed pages spread open to a new page yet to be read.

You pick up the journal, your gaze sweeping across the drawings on the wall... Finally, you understand why Graves didn't want you to see any of this. Childish handwriting accompanies each faded drawing on the wall, and together they tell a complete story about a "little monster."
[Enter Small CG 1 Flashback]
I was abandoned here.

I don't remember the rain that day. All I know is a scene roughly pieced together from what Sister Elsie told me—on a night with no cradle or hugs, a little monster was left all alone on cold stone steps, forgotten in the wind and rain.
Sister Elsie told me that the night was bitterly cold, where the sound of rain falling on the vines outside echoed like weeping.

steps.speaker: Nun
steps.content: But you didn't cry.
That's what she said.

steps.speaker: Nun
steps.content: You didn't make even the slightest whimper. Frighteningly quiet, as if you somehow knew no one would ever come.
Later, I asked her, "Who left me here?"
She just shook her head and said she didn't know.
Then why did they leave me here? I asked again.

steps.speaker: Nun
steps.content: ...Because you are a <color=#fb9259>special</color> child.
What does "special" mean? I don't understand.
Maybe it means I did something wrong, and now I have to do lots and lots of good things to make up for it. Only then would someone come to take me home.
But now I have a new question: What is "home"?
[End of Flashback]

The Mania storm draws closer, with surging dark mist seeping through the cracks, a foreboding sign urging you to leave. You pick up the journal and turn away, but the childish handwriting chronicling the past has already etched itself into your memory, its silent confessions echoing within you.
[Enter Small CG 2 Flashback]
I made my first rag doll. Just as Sister Elsie had named me, I gave her a name too.

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: I'll call you "Little Graves."
I made her body from the old hall curtains that had just been replaced, carved her hands and feet from kitchen spoons, and drew big eyes and rosy lips on her face.
That day was also the first time I got brave enough to step outside the castle.

steps.speaker: Child
steps.content: Monster! Monster! Get lost!

steps.speaker: Child
steps.content: We hate you! Stay away from us!

steps.speaker: Child
steps.content: You look disgusting! Freak!
I don't think they like my Little Graves.
But what does "monster" mean? I learn things really slowly. The only word I've learned lately is "friend."
I wanted to be friends with them, but they knocked my doll to the ground. Someone even stepped on her. I heard the wood crack and the fabric rip.
Little Graves was broken.
My hands are too clumsy—that must be why. My doll wasn't pretty enough. Next time, I'll try harder to make her look nicer.
[End of Flashback] [Intense tremor in the hallway]

Returning to the hallway with the journal clutched in hand, you find that the once sinister space has shed its eerie facade. The monsters, who were rehearsing wedding speeches, have vanished along with the disorienting maze that ensnared you.

The shattered hallway no longer blocks your way. A clear, straight path has emerged amidst the collapsed ruins. The remaining stone tiles, toppled pillars, and shattered window frames all seem to align, wordlessly guiding you in one direction—toward the ceremony hall, where Graves now awaits.
[Enter Small CG 3 Flashback]
So that's why Sister Elsie wouldn't let me near the hall—because they held something called a "wedding" there.

steps.speaker: Groom
steps.content: I vow to stand by your side, in life and in death, in darkness and in light, and never to part from you...
So people can be brave... they can stand close to each other without running away... they can hold hands tight and promise for sure—"never to part from you."
Watching them exchange rings, receive blessings, and hug tightly while everyone clapped and cheered... my heart was beating so fast.
The bride's dress was so pretty. Everyone gave her their blessings.
Wedding—I've learned this word now. It sounds happier and like it lasts longer than "friend" or "home."
[End of Flashback]
Luminita crouches behind the last pillar still standing. Beside her, No. 15 and Dullahan lie unconscious.

Talismans, copper coins, peach wood swords, crucifixes, holy water, parchment scrolls... her bag lies completely empty now. As the bride, clad in a dress weaved by resentment, draws near alongside the tempestuous storm, Luminita can only offer prayers to every deity she knows, hoping that someone returns quickly.
[Flashback]
That was my first wedding dress. Even though it was made from rags, I thought it was the prettiest dress in the whole world.
I walked out wearing it. I was sure they'd think I looked pretty, that they'd like me just like everyone likes a bride.
But they just laughed... They threw stones at me. The dress got caught and torn by the stones.
I looked down at my dress, now dirty and torn, and thought about my broken doll.

steps.speaker: Graves?
steps.content: I'm a monster! No one will ever like me!

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: Don't say that! Someone will. I will have my own wedding someday!
I started arguing with my other self. After that, we argued a lot.
[End of Flashback]

Graves, consumed completely by her negative persona, now wears an eerie smile on her face. Arms outstretched in a twisted embrace of the darkness, she moves with an unsettling grace. Alone, she glides through the debris, twirling and bowing, head inclined and wrists raised as if in a macabre dance with an unseen companion.

The battered hallway becomes her ballroom, the storm her symphony. Deathly silence envelops the surroundings, with only her dress billowing in the breath of Mania as she performs her solitary, unanswered waltz.
[Flashback]

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: Look what I found!

steps.speaker: Graves?
steps.content: A ring?
The ring is so pretty, but my hands... they're red and rough, with long nails like claws.
An ugly monster doesn't deserve happiness. Only if you're pretty enough will someone say, "I vow to never part with you, in life and in death."

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: Help me. We can have happiness right away.
This ring is magic. It helped me hide my other self. I also used it to hide this room.
This way I won't be "special" anymore.
I think maybe this time will be different. Maybe... I can finally be a happy bride, just like in the stories.
[End of Flashback]
